claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Adding a controlled amount of Zr to HfMoTaTiZr could reduce its density.
Zr addition can retain the mechanical properties of HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature.
Zr addition can retain the mechanical properties of HfMoTaTiZr at elevated temperatures, including approximately 1000 °C.
Zr addition produces solid-solution strengthening in HfMoTaTiZr.
The alloying effect of added Zr changes the microstructure of HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed intervention is applicable from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The exact amount of Zr needed to reduce density without compromising mechanical properties is uncertain.
Density, tensile strength, and ductility can be compared between the baseline and Zr-modified samples at room temperature and 1000 °C.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is existential and allows that only some controlled Zr amount may work, but the rejection rule says that failure of any tested Zr-added sample falsifies it. A single unsuitable addition level does not refute the possibility that another controlled level satisfies the hypothesis.
